Ivys has gone all out, severing his connection with Kairos, and becoming a lone replicant again. He is essentially an electronic device, let's use a laptop as an example. He has a battery, and without Kairos he has no charger. He doesn't turn off and die immediately when he is unplugged, but slowly he loses battery life, his screen grows dark and the OS recommends turning on power saving mode. Ivys is headed to power saving mode very quickly.
He does not have long left to live unless he does something, less than a year for sure. He can make an arcana check to discern the effects and their depth: (on 10 and 15 he knows that his analysis is an educated guess at best, and its likely less than that maximum but it depends on his activity level and magic use during that time.)
- 10: You have at most 5 years
- 15: 2 years 
- 20+: 1 year at most.

This is not good for him, as he has plans and the world probably needs him for a while after this. He wants to stay alive, mainly to stop Kairos. How can he do this? There's a couple ways:
- **Karegor**. Karegor is highly knowledgeable about replicants, and could easily help Ivys double his expected lifespan, but it would cost him both his allegiance and his morals. Karegor would make Ivys forsake his duties as the White Wizard, and essentially would end the Wizards council as Ivys is the last member. Karegor is also a neutral evil actor meaning Ivys would be forced into wrongdoing. 
- **Demonic Rebirth**. Through the Voracian Rebirth Ritual (there are others he can look into but they are worse because they either tie his will to the demon or have a low success rate), is a powerful and dangerous ritual with a 20% success rate. This would bind a demons soul to Ivys granting him power but also severing him from Kairos, essentially giving him his own soul and life force, making him no longer decay as a replicant would. This ritual is outlined in the academic text: [[The Blood of the Reborn]]
- **The One Who Casts**. While they are an enigmatic entity, they are the sibling and parallel to Karegor, and where Karegor harbors weakness and a desperate need for knowledge, TOWC is the embodiment of complacency. They are powerful and ok with that, if they were unpowerful they are ok with that, and they can give that to Ivys. He can make Ivys human, and that's all, he just wants Ivys to stop needing more, stop fighting, and let the world run its course (which hopefully Ivys won't do).

Prioritize him towards the Rebirth angle, as that's what Hunter expressed interest in doing most. It's the only real option that solves his issue anyway.

How does this end with Kairos? Before they fight Kairos at some point, in exchange for doing Karegor's quest and giving him the nature and secret of the Curse of Etrastrife, he will tell Ivys about the nature of his existence.
Ivys is **not** a Kairos replicant. Horus ran out of alternate versions and sections of himself to pull from, and instead made a replicant based on Kairos' daughter. Ivys is Lisa, he is literally Kairos' son.
Revealing this information is painful, confusing, and disorienting to Kairos, but it unlocks something that was long lost until now: A piece of his humanity, and a chance for forgiveness. In that moment of learning, he cares not for revenge, for being a god, or anything other than Ivys, and he simply asks him to come with him, to talk, and to live, to begin to fix what he had wronged, but it means Ivys has to leave behind his world and his friends. Ivys hopefully accepts to stop Kairos, and they depart. This will be very emotional in game, with kairos crying as he realizes what hes done in the name of his child who he though was lost, but was there all along. He begs Ivys to come with him, desperate for respite from the millennia of pain he has been feeling.
